title: Choose Athena Studio's visual direction
question: The first surface is the no-code operational UI builder for an image-detection project. Keep the assigned direction, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Inspection Tag System
options.lineage: Japanese manufacturing inspection and disposition labels
options.thesis: A confident label hierarchy makes every operator decision legible and traceable.
options.viewport: A familiar project shell holds a live operational-screen preview in the center and guided layout settings beside it; the same clear label hierarchy appears in annotation, model, and operator-decision states.
options.risk: A stamp-like mark could imply a final legal verdict; show human review and never style model output as certification.

raised.raise: Keep destructive project and model actions isolated from routine operator controls.
Expose readable dataset and model version IDs; never encode meaning in color blocks alone.

options.label: Tokyo Rail Wayfinding
options.lineage: Japanese rail network maps and station wayfinding
options.thesis: One progress line traces how a labeled sample becomes an approved live model.
options.viewport: Standard project navigation and controls stay familiar; a single horizontal route line links Label, Train, Configure, and Run, while the live operator-screen preview and its source/model provenance lead the work area.
options.risk: A route line can become decorative transit cosplay; keep it to one progress/provenance cue and retain text labels and ordinary controls.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.thesis: Panel seams and deliberate action spacing prioritize safe system operation.
options.viewport: A standard project shell shows status and model controls in compact panels; destructive actions sit alone behind deliberate confirmation.
options.case: The safety discipline is useful, but the developer-console look misidentifies a product for nontechnical industry operators.
options.kept: Isolate destructive project/model actions from everyday controls.
options.risk: Reads technical and intimidating to the intended operator.

options.label: Numbered Contact-Sheet Catalog
options.lineage: Japanese event catalogs and postage-stamp image grids
options.thesis: A whole-cell image catalog makes a growing reviewed dataset easy to scan.
options.viewport: A standard project shell surrounds a numbered image-contact sheet, each cell carrying a readable class and review state; selecting a cell opens its full annotation and provenance.
options.case: Strong for image-heavy dataset discovery and sample navigation; weaker for the trained model and deployed interface workflow.
options.risk: Dense thumbnails become unreadable on narrow screens; repack only in whole cells and preserve a list view.

options.label: Layered Technical Manual
options.lineage: Japanese technical manuals and annotated cutaway plates
options.thesis: Separating source image, human annotation, and model result makes provenance visible.
options.viewport: The familiar app shell keeps navigation and controls; the center preview layers the original scan, human box annotations, and model output with explicit labels and independent visibility controls.
options.case: The overlay model clarifies source-versus-human-versus-model evidence; the manual's document-led form loses to the assigned operator workflow.
options.risk: Layer toggles can be confused with visibility of the source itself; name each layer and retain an always-available raw view.

options.label: Coded Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Compact codes make a large model and dataset catalog feel precise.
options.viewport: A standard shell keeps a model registry and one live-preview panel, using stable version codes as the primary index.
options.case: The coded-artifact look loses both operator identification and immediate task clarity.
options.kept: Make dataset/model version identifiers stable, visible, and copyable.
options.risk: Color strips and abbreviated IDs hide meaning from nontechnical users.

options.label: Color-Region Guide Map
options.thesis: A small number of color-coded work areas make project progress feel approachable.
options.viewport: A conventional shell remains intact; one generous work area shows dataset, training, and live-interface status as clearly named colored regions, never as a replacement for labels or controls.
options.case: The approachable color grouping helps a novice understand project areas; it is less suited to detailed image review and technical provenance.
options.risk: Color alone must never identify class or state; pair every region with a text label and icon/shape.

options.label: Live Variable Specimen
options.lineage: Interactive type specimens and Japanese type-design publishing
options.thesis: Every safe configuration change immediately reshapes the real operational-screen preview.
options.viewport: A standard project shell presents guided settings beside a live, full-screen operator preview; edits to labels, layout, and thresholds update the preview and named feedback states together.
options.case: The live specimen is a direct metaphor for no-code UI customization and gives nontechnical operators immediate proof of each change.
options.risk: A typography-first look could minimize the underlying industrial task; keep detected image states and provenance larger than decorative type.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The expected industrial project dashboard, executed with complete clarity.
canonCard.viewport: Conventional sidebar, project header, readable status cards, an ordinary configuration form, and a well-sized live preview with explicit states.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and easy to scan, but less distinctive than the grounded visual systems.
